characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Fischerscope H100 microhardness tester (maximum load 1 N)
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 300 °C/6 h anneal gives the same hardness as the as-grown monocrystal; heat treatment shifts HU by only about 5–10% (data scatter tightly about the 2000 N/mm² gridline).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; HU = F/(26.43·h²) [N/mm²]; averages of more than 40 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: to study the effect of prior heat treatment (state of atomic/short-range order) on the hardness of the (111)-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal

characterization_methods.key_findings: The rare globular inclusions (up to 30 µm diameter) in the monocrystals were identified as AlN.
characterization_methods.purpose: identification of the rare globular inclusions in the monocrystals

processing_steps.duration: about 12 h (crystal growth with subsequent cooling)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Monocrystals with up to 10 cm length grown by the Bridgman method; yields the as-grown Fe-16%Al monocrystal (16.0 at.% Al, 8.4 wt.-%; 45 wt.ppm C, 40 wt.ppm Si, 60 wt.ppm O). This as-grown crystal is the starting material for the 300 °C/6 h anneal.

One of a series of 300 °C anneals of different durations applied to the (111)-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal for the microhardness study (Fig. 1). The short heat treatments at temperatures up to 300 °C occurred in an argon atmosphere with 99.99% purity. The 6 h anneal gives an intermediate degree of short-range order (between the minimum ordering after quenching from 1100 or 600 °C and the maximum ordering after 250 °C/14 days) and produces the same hardness as the as-grown monocrystal.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Microhardness tester Fischerscope H100 with maximum load 1 N; universal hardness HU = F/(26.43·h²) [N/mm²]; reported HU values are averages of more than 40 measurements.

inclusions: AlN, up to 30 µm diameter, identified by EDX

grain_structure.texture: (111) orientation of the Fe-16%Al monocrystal specimens

microstructure_list.region: bulk monocrystal (specimens used for microhardness, Fig. 1)

structures.overall_structure: (111)-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal, essentially single-phase (no second phases/precipitates reported for this heat treatment) with an intermediate degree of short-range order (K-state) resulting from the 300 °C/6 h anneal; contains rare globular AlN inclusions.

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-16%Al monocrystal, the 300 °C/6 h anneal produces the same hardness as the as-grown monocrystal and corresponds to an intermediate degree of short-range order — between the minimum ordering after quenching from 1100 or 600 °C and the maximum ordering after a 250 °C/14-day anneal (b0050).

The hardness of the Fe-16%Al monocrystal does not depend sensitively on heat treatment: the Fig. 1 data vary by only about 10% at most around ~2000 N/mm², and no major impact of short-range ordering on hardness was found (b0029, b0050, figure_001).
No carbides were detected in the Fe-16%Al monocrystal with 45 ppm C after a heat treatment of 14 days at 320 °C, and without heat treatment no carbides were found in all monocrystals (b0026).
Short heat treatments at temperatures up to 300 °C (including 300 °C/6 h) were performed in an argon atmosphere of 99.99% purity, whereas other heat treatments used evacuated SiO2 capsules (b0015).
